<notes>
kept -> base harness -> all 3 base rollouts delivered identical correct answers (358,803) with identical arithmetic at each step; all 6 candidate rollouts (identical to base harness per their diffs) also delivered the same correct answer; no divergence observed (unlike holdout-numeric-002 where base1 was wrong and base2/3 correct, or holdout-numeric-005 where bases diverged), no repeated concrete failure, no trajectory moment where the LLM failed to calculate or where a different harness would have changed the outcome. Library precedents (holdout-numeric-002, holdout-numeric-005) apply specifically to tasks where base runs showed divergence or failure—neither condition holds here. Mission guidance: "Do not fix what the runs already got right" and "Every edit must trace to a moment in a trajectory. For each one ask: which run did what, and would this text have changed it? If you cannot name the moment, the edit is speculation." No such moment exists. Adding code extraction and instruction would be always-on overhead on a task the current harness already solves correctly and consistently.
</notes>

KEEP_BASE
